rows.title: Policy divergence
rows.read: USD-supportive: Hammack (Cleveland Fed) says inflation is broad-based and policy must stay restrictive; Oct hike ~19–22%, Dec ~75–85% (feed-dependent) — the hawkish hold is in week five; CPI Wed 7:30am CT is the test, Warsh speaks Thu 10:30pm CT.

sources.label: Barchart: Dollar rallies to 1.5-yr high on crude + Hammack (Oct 12)
DeFi Rate: Fed decision odds aggregate, prediction markets (Oct 12)

rows.title: Growth
rows.read: US resilient, Canada cracking, China reopening soft — the growth gaps all favor the dollar; oil's +2% is a tax on importers (Japan, Europe) and a tailwind for Canada that the 161bp gap keeps cancelling.

sources.label: Reuters: Dollar steady near 18-month high, Mideast conflict in focus (Oct 12)
TradingNews: EUR/USD near 17-mo low as French spread, 175bp gap bite (Oct 12)

rows.title: Inflation
rows.read: Headline risk, core watch — US CPI Wed 7:30am CT (consensus ~3.6% y/y, core m/m ~0.2%, core y/y ~2.5%), the last big print before the Oct 27–28 FOMC; Hammack: inflation pressures are broad-based, not concentrated.

rows.title: Risk sentiment
rows.read: The ceasefire died and the rally lived — Brent settled $106.65 (+1.8%) on Gulf escalation (Houthi strikes, tanker hits); DXY printed a 1.5-year high; CBA expects Houthi attacks on Saudi energy assets to continue.

rows.title: Terms of trade
rows.read: The ~$13 Brent–WTI spread keeps the geopolitical-premium gauge wide; WTI ~$93.8 is the CAD read; Goldman sees just over $20/bbl of premium with Dec Brent at $90; OPEC cut 2026 demand growth to 400k bpd.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.read: Bullish dollar bets jumped to ~$36bn (week to Oct 7, from $8.4bn three weeks ago) — largely at the euro's expense; crowded USD longs into Wednesday's CPI is the squeeze risk. Yen longs sat at 62,325 into escalation.

rows.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk
rows.read: French budget plenary Tuesday 3:00am CT is the live fuse — OAT–Bund spiked to 152bp (widest since 2011), sitting ~134–140 into the debate; debt ~119% of GDP toward 122%; record €340bn borrowing in 2027. The euro waits.
